request.prompt: Standing on wet shingle at the foot of a low cliff, looking inland and south. A wrecked timber jetty runs out to the left into the water, its piles snapped. Straight ahead the shingle ends against a stone sea wall with a flight of steps cut into it. Beyond the wall, up on its terrace, the long slate roof and four square chimneys of a stone boiling house. Far off to the right, at the end of a headland, one small warm lamp burning in a squat tower. An open boat is drawn up on the shingle behind the eye.
request.style_note: The Saltworks at Greyhithe, in one hand throughout: a cold North Sea dusk, the sky a narrow band of pale light low in the west and dark above. One masonry everywhere — grey lias limestone laid in long thin courses, iron-stained red-brown where the sea reaches it, quoins and jambs in the same stone dressed square. One way of letting light in — tall narrow round-headed openings in a repeated rhythm, high in the wall, in the works and in the abbey alike. Slate roofs weathered near-black, salt-bleached timber, no render, no whitewash. One warm lamp burning on the headland, the only warm colour in the picture. Matte gouache on toned grey paper, restrained palette, visible dry brush, no figures, no text, no lettering. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset or a caption.
